about.title: Los Banos Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Los Banos sits at the crossroads of agriculture, logistics, and retail work, which means the ways people get hurt on the job here vary widely, from equipment accidents on farms near Rt 165 to slip-and-falls in warehouses off E Pacheco Boulevard. Under California law, workers' compensation is typically the exclusive remedy against your employer no matter who was at fault, but that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate legal path outside the workers' comp system. Navigating both systems at once can be confusing, especially while you're trying to recover and worried about your paycheck. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that connects injured workers in Los Banos with independent attorneys who can help sort out which claims apply to your situation and represent you on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Workplace Injury

items.title: Third-Party Claims May Exist Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Workers' comp usually bars a lawsuit against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, equipment maker, or another driver may still be liable. An attorney can help identify whether a separate claim applies to your case.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim. An attorney can help make sure the right steps are documented on time.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: It's against California law for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can advise you on your rights.

items.question: I was hurt driving for work near E Pacheco Boulevard. Do I only have a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: Not necessarily. If another driver caused the collision while you were working, you may have a workers' comp claim against your employer and a separate third-party injury claim against that driver. An independent attorney can review the details and explain how the two claims interact.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a workplace injury in Los Banos?
items.answer: You generally need to report the injury to your employer within 30 days to preserve your workers' comp rights. If a third party is involved, California law generally allows two years from the date of injury to file that separate claim. Because deadlines can vary by claim type, it's worth talking to an attorney soon after the injury.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workplace injury claim?
items.answer: No, California law prohibits retaliation against employees for reporting a workplace injury or pursuing a workers' comp claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an attorney can help you understand your options. LawProactive can connect you with someone who handles these situations regularly.
